text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - German Bunds slid to losses in late trade on Wednesday as sentiment received knocks from a fall in U.S. Treasuries and the market's repeated failure to breach key resistance, dealers said. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.13 down 0.43 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts endured a heavy fall on Wednesday afternoon, ending more than a point lower, as a break of key support levels triggered a wave of profit-taking. Dealers said correction was well overdue. Earlier, PSBR and jobs data pushed the market lower. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-17/32, down 1-8/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures slid sharply to day lows at the close of MATIF trading, in line with a trend in other European centres and after a topsy-turvy day marked by rumours at one stage of a delay in European monetary union. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 125.84, down 0.60 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds, futures and currency took a late hammering after Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer reiterated his view that one-off measures would not be enough to qualify for EMU, which he expected to start on time in 1999. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 121.50, down 1.65 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were sharply lower in moderate midday trade Wednesday as a combination of factors dragged prices down after a brief relief rally that followed the release of a key inflation gauge. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-30/32, down 18/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.9 percent.

JAPAN - Key December Japanese government bond futures ended sharply lower as selling was triggered by a local news agency report that a senior member of the Liberal Democratic Party, said a supplementary budget worth about five trillion yen must be considered at a special parliamentary session after general elections on October 20. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 122.52, down 0.53 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market got off to a slower start as the Euromarket digested Tuesday's barrage of bonds. Activity continued in the highly popular lira sector with the Council of Europe launching a 200 bln lire 5-year bond. In sterling, the EIB set a 300 million stg Dec 2003 bond while Abbey National added 250 million stg to its 6.0 pct August 1999 bond. Nordbanken set a $100 million perpetual step-up subordinated FRN which is callable every five years via Chase. Other activity spanned Australian and New Zealand dollars.
